prompt.context: Our client is a major US television network that is trying to figure out how much to bid for the 2018 Winter Olympics and has brought you in to help figure out the right bid. The Winter Olympics are a huge deal and will require a significant amount of capital to secure the rights. Before our network bids on the Winter Olympics, we want to make sure that we've considered all the right things.
prompt.question: How much should our client bid for the 2018 Winter Olympics broadcasting rights?

clarifying_info.q: What is the schedule for the Winter Olympics?
clarifying_info.a: 16 days total. Day 1 (Friday): Opening ceremonies, 3 hours of programming 8-11 PM. Days 2-15: Games, 10 hours/day (Weekdays: 9-12, 2-5, 7-11; Weekends: 11 AM-9 PM). Day 16 (Saturday): Closing ceremonies, 3 hours of programming 8-11 PM.

No subscription revenue. The network keeps 100% of advertising revenue. Ad rates are $400K per 30-second ad for prime time (M-F 7-11 PM, all weekend) and $200K per ad for non-prime time. Market research shows no more than 10 minutes of advertising per hour.
Total production costs are $428M. Opportunity cost is $1M per hour of programming. There is a 6-year lag for receipt of revenue, and the WACC is 12%.

framework: Identify total advertising revenues by time slot (prime time vs. non-prime time, weekday vs. weekend, opening/closing)
Calculate total direct costs (production costs + opportunity costs)
Apply time value of money (NPV adjustment using WACC and 6-year lag)
Assess intangible factors: new viewers, prestige, cross-promotion, supplemental revenue
Determine final bid recommendation relative to NPV, with justification for any premium

questions.prompt: Calculate the total advertising revenue from broadcasting the Winter Olympics.
questions.guidance: Candidate should break down programming into distinct time blocks (prime weekday, non-prime weekday, weekend, opening/closing) and apply the correct ad rate and slot count to each. 30-second ads = 2 slots per minute; 10 min of ads per hour.

math.setup: Break programming into four segments: (1) Prime time weekdays, (2) Non-prime time weekdays, (3) Weekends, (4) Opening/Closing ceremonies. Each segment: [days] x [hours/day] x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x [rate/slot].
steps: Prime time weekdays (M-F, 7-11 PM): 10 days x 4 hrs/day x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x $400K = $320M
Non-prime time weekdays (M-F, 9-12 and 2-5): 10 days x 6 hrs/day x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x $200K = $240M
Weekend days (Days 2-15 include 4 weekend days, 10 hrs/day): 4 days x 10 hrs/day x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x $400K = $320M
Opening/Closing ceremonies (2 days x 3 hrs, prime time rate): 2 days x 3 hrs/day x 10 min/hr x 2 slots/min x $400K = $48M

questions.prompt: Factoring in all costs, what is the NPV of the investment? Is this a good investment?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify three cost categories: (1) direct production costs, (2) opportunity costs from displacing existing programming, and (3) time value of money via a WACC discount. Use the Rule of 72 to apply the discount.

math.setup: NPV = (Revenues - Production costs - Opportunity costs) discounted for time value of money. Opportunity cost = $1M/hr x total programming hours. Time value: use Rule of 72 with 12% WACC and 6-year lag to determine that money doubles in ~6 years, so future cash flows should be halved.
steps: Opportunity cost: Opening/Closing (2 days x 3 hrs x $1M/hr = $6M) + Games (14 days x 10 hrs x $1M/hr = $140M) = $146M
Rule of 72: 72 / 12% = 6 years to double; with a 6-year lag, halve the result: $354M / 2 = $177M
math.answer: NPV = $177M; this is a positive NPV and therefore a worthwhile investment at the right bid price

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond the NPV of $177M, what intangible factors and other considerations should influence the final bid amount?

categories.name: Audience & Reach
ideas: Access to new viewers who may not normally watch the network
Olympics attract a broad demographic including light TV viewers
Potential to convert Olympics viewers to regular network viewers

categories.name: Brand & Prestige
ideas: Significant prestige associated with hosting a major global sporting event
Strengthens the network's brand image and positioning
Signal to advertisers and partners of network quality

categories.name: Cross-Promotion
ideas: Can use air time during the Olympics to promote other programming
Opportunity to announce upcoming shows to a large captive audience
Drive viewership for the rest of the season

categories.name: Supplemental Revenue
ideas: Product tie-ins and sponsorship deals beyond standard advertising
Digital/streaming rights and secondary platform monetization

categories.name: Competitive & Game Theory
ideas: Consider how many other networks are bidding and their likely bid levels
Risk of overpaying if bid too aggressively versus losing rights
Strategic value of blocking a competitor from securing the rights

categories.name: Downside Risks
ideas: Low viewership if key sports or athletes underperform
Political controversies or boycotts affecting ratings
Production cost overruns beyond the $428M estimate
Currency and inflation risk given 6-year timeline

recommendation: The NPV of the broadcasting rights is $177M, representing the floor for a rational bid
Accounting for intangible benefits (new viewers, prestige, cross-promotion, supplemental revenues), the recommended bid is approximately $200M
The bid should not significantly exceed $200M without a strong strategic rationale, as the financial case is anchored at $177M
risks: Competitor bids may force the price above financial breakeven
Actual viewership could underperform projections, reducing ad revenue
Production cost overruns could erode the NPV margin
A 6-year lag introduces uncertainty in both revenue realization and cost estimates
next_steps: Conduct competitive intelligence on likely competing bids from other networks
Model sensitivity of NPV to viewership and ad rate assumptions
Identify and quantify supplemental revenue opportunities (streaming, sponsorships) to better calibrate any premium above NPV
Define a walk-away price and ensure internal alignment before entering the auction
